Will Evernorth’s Nasdaq Listing Push XRP Price Higher?

Evernorth entered Nasdaq holding approximately 473 million XRP, worth around $648 million at Monday’s token price of $1.37. The company also reported roughly $300 million in gross cash proceeds before expenses.
However, the listing does not automatically create fresh buying pressure for XRP.

According to SEC filings, much of Evernorth’s treasury came from investors contributing existing XRP in exchange for equity. Buying XRPN shares on Nasdaq does not directly trigger purchases of the cryptocurrency.
Meanwhile, XRP itself fell 3.03% over 24 hours, showing that the Wall Street debut failed to reverse the token’s weakness.
The bigger question is how Evernorth uses its capital. CEO Asheesh Birla said the company would pursue strategies designed to “grow XRP per share over time.”
New XRP purchases could create demand and support prices. Strong demand for XRPN shares could also help Evernorth raise additional capital to expand its treasury.
However, sustained weakness in the stock could make fundraising harder.

For now, XRP’s direction remains tied more closely to broader crypto market conditions. Investors should watch whether Evernorth announces actual token purchases rather than relying on its Nasdaq debut as a bullish signal.

title: The Largest XRP Treasury Goes Public, but Its Nasdaq Debut Ends in Red
